schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The BUILD skill: the stage after the preamble, fired as /sail <something>. FIRES /chart AS ITS OWN STEP 0 (Akien, 2026-08-14: 'slash sail should just start with slash chart') and then consumes that chain's berths (template-fills from the deepest berthed stage; refuses to build from the conversation), requires a cast ticket (/sorted owns casting, and still runs BEFORE /sail because the chart doors refuse a claim on an unfiled ticket), and runs the voyage discipline as numbered skill-steps: journal BUILDME -> build inside the bounds (constrain = hard edges, survey holdings = compose, absences = build-minimal) -> prove twice -> PROVEME + tester seal -> live fire -> PROVED + records settled -> deposit learnings AND the tool-call findings the build owes the chain -> commit/push verified by instrument -> close the boundary with /saveslate then an invitation to /compact (a client command the skill cannot fire; making the boundary loud IS the step).
why: Akien, 2026-07-28, verbatim: 'we still need a build skill, whatever it shall be called... according to you in the web interface, we should simply add /compact to the end of /sorted and the new build skill' + 'i might suggest we also have a /saveslate before the compact'. The deep why is the ratified pattern from the daemons correction: CC-discipline moves into skill-STEPS, not personal habit (Law 4) — the whole build liturgy (chokepoint crossings, prove-twice, seal, live fire, deposit-back, commit-is-done) has lived in CC's habit and memory files, varying with the session; behind the slash-door it fires the same way every time. The /saveslate-then-/compact close makes the compaction boundary SAFE by construction: the slate is the durable half, so the context being dropped is provably scaffolding. NAMING: /sail is CC's coinage, flagged as such (terms-drift discipline) — you chart a course, then you sail it; sits beside chart/charter/voyage/berth/harbor in the ship vocabulary, and the record already calls the BUILDME->PROVED journey a VOYAGE, which /sail runs. RATIFIED 2026-07-28, Akien: 'sail. i like that.' — the name is settled.
invoke: /sail <request> (symlinked ~/.claude/skills/sail -> repo skills/sail). Requires a cast ticket; does NOT require berthed /chart packets, because step 0 makes them. /chart remains separately invocable for a preamble without a voyage.

feedback.why: AKIEN'S DIRECTION, 2026-08-14, verbatim: /sail 'runs in sail, gets feedback about tool calls that happen inside the build. and we add that feedback into our mechanisms.' The segment shape with the BUILD as the machine: the chart chain is the upstream creative entity, its berths are this skill's whole input, and the tool calls are the ONLY place its claims meet the world. survey names what exists and what is absent; constrain names the hard edges; orient names where the work lives. A build that opens a file survey never listed, writes outside constrain's bounds, or rebuilds a holding survey had already found has just measured one of those claims and found it wrong — and this skill's OWN falsifier already names two of the three ('a bound from the constrain berth silently widened; a holding rebuilt in parallel'), which is the fact that makes this a route rather than an idea: the findings were already specified, they simply had nowhere to go. CORRECTED BY RULING 2026-08-14-the-preamble-compiles-to-learn-not-to-be-cheap, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE SHAPE OF THE SIGNAL. The paragraph above describes per-claim falsification — each finding naming the berth field it contradicted — and that is not the first mechanism. Akien: 'you can score the quality of the information downward just by doing more tool calls before the build is done. the system learns from you.' THE SIGNAL IS CALL VOLUME BETWEEN THE PACKET AND DONE, scored downward. It is one number, already emitted by every voyage, and it needs no adjudication of what counts as a contradiction — which dissolves the firehose problem rather than solving it, because nothing is being classified. The claim-anchored findings above are kept, not deleted, because they remain the right SECOND thing: a score says the packet was bad, never which field was. But the score is what is built first and what this route carries. WHY THE CHAIN AND NOT A LEG: the finding's subject names its leg exactly — bound widened is constrain's, holding rebuilt is survey's, wrong address is orient's — and one address cannot say that. That is not this charter's call to make; it is ticket a-segments-outbound-edge-carries-one-address, option (2), and this is the clearest case for it yet measured, because here the subject is unambiguous rather than inferred. Until he settles the shape, the route names the chain that holds all seven legs, and a finding written at step 9 names its leg in its own text. WHAT IS NOT BUILT AND IS NOT PRETENDED: nothing observes the tool calls, so the findings are a hand's at step 9 (ticket the-builds-tool-calls-are-evidence-about-the-chart), and nothing delivers along the -2- edge for anyone yet (cairn/tools/feedback edge (a)). A declared route with no producer and no deliverer is the design recorded, not a mechanism running — see filed edge (e).

node_class: skill — prose-as-implementation in class-space; the standing host-seam pattern (repo skills/ + symlink) carries it; hangs the cairnmap recompile gate like every skill node.
entry: FRESH, 2026-07-28, cast the same day /chart reached three stages — the chain finally emits enough settled input for the build stage to template-fill from.
state_and_history: voyage journaled on the chart device (the chain it completes); this charter stays pure intention+why.
how_it_learns: Through the bricks it composes, not privately: every /sail crossing deposits its berths back (step 7), corrections ride orient's brick loop, and build failures seed inspector filters by installation. The skill's own prose sharpens by /challenge like every skill; a recurring deviation between the steps and what CC actually does is the signal the prose is wrong or the discipline needs physics (the gate ladder: prose -> skill-step -> chokepoint).
filed_edges: (a) the middle stages (decompose/triage/hypothesize/validate) land between /chart and /sail as bricks; /sail then fills from a deeper chain without changing shape
(b) a /sail proof (skills/sail/proofs/) pinning the refusal contract — no berths / no ticket — once the skill has enough crossings to know its real failure modes
(c) the /saveslate-then-/compact close is also /sorted's close (same ruling, same act) — if a third skill wants it, the close becomes a shared fragment, earned not merged

(d) THE SECOND CHART RUN, dropped by its author and recorded so the reason is not re-derived. /sail was to fire the chain twice — once at the start, once mid-build — and the condition on the second was never 'a correction appeared'. Akien, 2026-08-14: 'we had put a condition on running it inside sail but that wasn't it, it was about how much had changed for that component since the first chart run was taken.' He then dropped it himself, in the same breath, and ranked it: 'this is too complicated, so we'll simplify to run at the start of sail only. the thing i wanted to accomplish by having two can be dealt with later. it's the least important part.' NOT TICKETED, deliberately, and the ranking is why — the person who wants it called it the least important part, so a ticket would be CC manufacturing a priority he had just declined to assign. It is written here so that a later reader who rediscovers the idea finds it already considered, already scoped (a drift measure per component, not a correction trigger), and already deferred by name. NOTE THE DISTINCTION IT TURNS ON: feedback firing mid-build is UNCHANGED and still fires (step 9); what was dropped is a second run of the CHAIN.

(e) THE ROUTE BELOW IS DECLARED AHEAD OF ITS PRODUCER, which `./bin/cmd/feedbackmap` cannot see and should not be read as covering. That instrument's population is components whose SHIPPED CODE calls gate.proved or the chain's inspected; this skill is markdown and calls neither, so the route is inert to it — a declaration, not a measured seal. It is written now because the design was ruled now, and the alternative is remembering it later.
gates: the /challenge cadence (skill prose); the recompile gate on charter writes; the REAL gate is downstream — every step it names is already enforced by physics where physics exists (chokepoint build gate, tester seal, berth doors), so the skill mostly cannot lie about having run them.
falsifier: RED on any of: a /sail build that filled from the conversation while berths existed; a bound from the constrain berth silently widened; a holding rebuilt in parallel; 'done' reported without the instrument's verification; the close skipped (no slate before a compact at a build boundary). WRONG-SHAPE SIGNAL: if /sail crossings routinely skip steps without a red anywhere, the discipline needs to move down the ladder from skill-step to physics.

counted_by.what_it_counts: NOTHING YET — but not for want of a record. A /sail that reaches step 6 writes a verdict artifact to instance/devices/chart/0/packets/verdict-*.json, and the emit chokepoint REFUSES the PROVED crossing without a complete, passing one (ExitGateRed). 32 of them stand there, the earliest 2026-07-29. So the firing record is not merely present, it is MANDATORY, and the roster's dash is a reader gap rather than a store gap.
counted_by.why_it_is_still_a_dash: cairn/machines/skill_block/counters.py::_read_files globs *.json in a directory and offers group_by_prefix, which GROUPS but does not FILTER. Pointing this charter at chart's packets dir today would count all 294 chart berths as /sail firings — a wrong number is worse than a dash, and the roster's own falsifier is that unmeasured must never be reported as measured. The reader needs a prefix filter; that is a build on a proved component, not a charter field.
counted_by.what_the_count_would_and_would_not_mean: A FLOOR. A verdict berth per voyage that reached PROVED — so a /sail that reads berths and builds nothing, or dies mid-voyage, still leaves nothing behind. It must declare that it undercounts, exactly as commit's git-trailer proxy declares that it overcounts. It does not fully close the complaint below; it closes the half that is measurable today.
counted_by.why_this_is_the_worst_place_for_a_gap: /sail is the BUILD step — the most expensive firing in the workflow and the only one that consumes a whole /chart chain. A /sail that reads berths and then builds nothing leaves the chain looking identical to a /sail that shipped. The step whose failure costs the most is the step we cannot see fail.
counted_by.corrected: 2026-08-11. This field used to read 'NOTHING. /sail is the one skill in the roster that leaves no firing record anywhere... no berth, no packet, no trace, no conforming commons record, no tree node' (measured 2026-08-04) and concluded 'it needs something built. That is a ticket, not a charter field.' Both were false: the packets existed on the day that was written. The 2026-08-04 repair that fixed five skills by declaring where their count ALREADY LIVED skipped the sixth — the one whose own charter called it the worst place for the hole. Akien, 2026-08-11: 'sounds like sail needs an update to remove that text.' The retired text is kept in decisions/2026-08-11-review-the-skills-and-workflow-monthly.json, which is where the error is permanent; a charter states the design as it now stands.

proof: PROVED 2026-07-28 by the first real crossing: the voyage that delivered decompose (tickets decompose-filters + chart-decompose) ran every step end to end — charted from berths (never the conversation), built inside the bounds, proved twice, sealed, live-fired, records settled, learnings deposited, commit instrument-verified, closed with slate + invitation. The constituent physics (chokepoint, tester, doors) stands proven where it lives; edge (b)'s refusal-contract proof still waits for enough crossings to know the real failure modes. Found in the crossing: the chokepoint refuses skill@v1 voyages (no registered workflow for class skill) — filed as ticket edge (d), RETIRED 2026-07-29 (ticket skills-ride-the-chokepoint): class skill@v1 is now registered at CairnCommons/node_classes/skill.json (the six summonses mirroring code-seam@v1's path verbatim, TICKETME skippable), zero changes to cairn/tools/base/transitions.py — the registry was the whole door. /sail's own record was then born by its first real journaled crossing (the live fire this stone owed): skills/sail/history.json + state.json, THINKME -> BUILDME, naming this same ticket, the entry gate clean over a berthed chart chain. The record starts mid-life — /sail proved out in prose a day before its record could exist — and every /sail crossing from here rides the chokepoint like any code-seam's.
